summary_hint: Donor <donor_name> (<relationship>) is gifting <borrower> $<gift_amount> for <subject property>, via <transfer_method>, [already transferred | pending], no repayment required. — a processor sees who gave what to whom and whether the three-link chain can close, without opening the PDF.

typed_core.name: issuer_name
typed_core.why: identity/source: the org that originated the letter/form (often the lender or a template provider); authenticity indicator

typed_core.name: donor_names_raw
typed_core.why: disambiguator — verbatim donor string so a bad split ('PAT AND ROBIN CHEN' = one or two donors) stays visible to the tag layer (bank_statement pattern); supports AS-5
typed_core.prompt_hint: Joint donors (two parents) are common — capture the verbatim donor_names_raw plus the split

typed_core.name: donor_name
typed_core.why: AS-5 — the donor-ability link: name must match the donor bank statement; identity

typed_core.name: donor_name_2
typed_core.why: AS-5 — joint donors (two parents common); identity of the second donor

typed_core.name: donor_relationship_to_borrower
typed_core.why: processor/eligibility: acceptable donor relationship (family) is a program requirement; feeds AS-5 gift validity
typed_core.prompt_hint: Acceptable donor relationships (family member, fiance, domestic partner) are eligibility-relevant — extract the relationship exactly as stated

typed_core.name: donor_address
typed_core.why: identity/attribution of the donor; potential PII (see PII) — flattened, not repeating

typed_core.name: donor_phone
typed_core.why: processor — independent donor verification / follow-up

typed_core.name: borrower_recipient_name
typed_core.why: AS-1 / AS-5 — whose deposit the gift matches; identity (attach to borrower)

typed_core.name: borrower_recipient_name_2
typed_core.why: identity — co-borrower recipient

typed_core.name: subject_property_address
typed_core.why: identity: links the letter to the subject property

typed_core.name: gift_amount
typed_core.why: AS-1 (compare to income-derived large-deposit threshold), AS-5 (match the gift to the deposit) — the primary matched value

typed_core.name: gift_date_or_expected_transfer_date
typed_core.why: AS-1 / AS-5 — match the deposit by date; distinguishes an executed vs expected transfer

typed_core.name: funds_already_transferred
typed_core.why: AS-5 — whether the transfer link already exists (transferred) or is still pending

typed_core.name: transfer_method
typed_core.why: AS-5 — transfer-evidence type (wire / check / ACH); disambiguator for matching the deposit
typed_core.prompt_hint: Typical transfer_method: wire, cashier's/certified check, personal check, ACH/EFT

typed_core.name: gift_source_account_institution
typed_core.why: AS-5 — donor-ability link: match the donor bank statement's institution

typed_core.name: gift_source_account_last4
typed_core.why: AS-5 — match the donor source account; PII (restricted, pre-masked last-4)
typed_core.prompt_hint: Two account numbers may appear — the donor's source account and the borrower's/escrow destination account. Emit last-4 for each into its own slot; never merge

typed_core.name: recipient_or_escrow_account_last4
typed_core.why: AS-1 / AS-5 — match the destination deposit account; PII (restricted, pre-masked last-4)

typed_core.name: gift_purpose
typed_core.why: disambiguator — down payment vs closing costs vs reserves tells AS-1 which deposit/use the gift funds
typed_core.prompt_hint: Typical gift_purpose values: down payment, closing costs, reserves

typed_core.name: no_repayment_required_statement
typed_core.why: the defining attestation (gift, not a disguised loan) that AS-5 exists to protect; keep verbatim text, not a bare bool
typed_core.prompt_hint: The no-repayment attestation is the field that makes the funds an asset rather than a debt — capture verbatim; if the letter does not state it, leave null, never invent

typed_core.name: no_ownership_or_lien_interest_statement
typed_core.why: AS-5 — reinforces gift-not-loan (donor retains no interest); verbatim

typed_core.name: lender_name
typed_core.why: identity — which loan/lender the gift is tied to; cross-document attribution

typed_core.name: document_issue_date
typed_core.why: identity/recency — the letter's own date (age testing)

typed_core.name: donor_signature_present
typed_core.why: AS-5 / processor — an unexecuted gift letter does not satisfy the chain link

typed_core.name: donor_signature_date
typed_core.why: processor — execution date of the donor signature

rejected.name: document_title
rejected.reason: weak identity; document_type comes from classification

rejected.name: form_number, form_revision_date
rejected.reason: gift letters are not a single standardized form

rejected.name: issuer_address, issuer_phone, issuer_email_or_url
rejected.reason: issuer of the form is rarely the actor; no rule/processor consumer

rejected.name: effective_date, expiration_date
rejected.reason: not applicable to a gift letter; would duplicate the gift date

rejected.name: statement_period_start, statement_period_end
rejected.reason: a gift letter has no statement period

rejected.name: party_names, party_addresses
rejected.reason: subsumed by the specific donor_/borrower_/subject fields

rejected.name: loan_number, account_case_reference_number
rejected.reason: rarely present; no rule reads a loan number on a gift letter

rejected.name: signature_blocks
rejected.reason: flattened to donor_signature_present/_date; a list is over-plumbing for one signature

rejected.name: notary_block
rejected.reason: gift letters are typically not notarized

rejected.name: borrower_acknowledgment_signature
rejected.reason: no consumer — the donor's execution is the link AS-5 checks

encoding_variations: Gift amount stated as $10,000 / 10,000.00 / Ten thousand dollars — coerce to Decimal; keep snippet.
Transfer state: 'funds have been transferred' vs 'will be transferred at closing' vs a checkbox — the bool degrades to str; disambiguate with transfer_method + gift_date_or_expected_transfer_date.
Donor source account referenced inline: 'drawn on Chase account ending 1234' — split into gift_source_account_institution + gift_source_account_last4; do not conflate with the recipient account.
No-repayment attestation phrased many ways ('no repayment is expected', 'not a loan', 'no obligation to repay') — capture verbatim str, null if truly absent.
Gift date may be the letter date, the deposit date, or an expected future date — the disambiguator is funds_already_transferred.

options: register donor_address in _PII_FIELDS (pre_masked=false) so it is masked + match-hashed like other addresses
open_questions.recommendation: register donor_address — a real address unmasked in the catch-all is the exact failure; leave donor_phone unregistered

open_questions.q: Joint donors shape. Flat donor_name / donor_name_2 + donor_names_raw covers 1-2 donors. If a rule ever needs to address 3+ donors individually, revisit as person[].
open_questions.recommendation: stay flat now; the raw string preserves recoverability

open_questions.q: no_repayment / no_ownership as str vs bool. No bool coercer exists, and the verbatim attestation is more useful for review than a stripped true/false.
open_questions.recommendation: keep as str (matches the existing extractor's no_repayment_attestation)

notes: donor_address flagged for review — recommendation is to register it in _PII_FIELDS (pre_masked=false) so a real residential address is not left unmasked in the catch-all; set here as ADDRESS/pre_masked=false pending reviewer sign-off. donor_phone (contact PII, standard sensitivity) left unregistered.

gift_source_account_last4 and recipient_or_escrow_account_last4 both need _PII_FIELDS registration (restricted, pre_masked=true; analogous to account_number_masked); today the donor and destination accounts land in the unmasked catch-all as PII.

Ambiguity: transfer_method — classed disambiguator (matches the 'disambiguator for matching the deposit' framing) with AS-5 in rules; a defensible alternative is reason_class rule since it is the AS-5 transfer-evidence type.
